newsitem.title: GERMANY: German call money eases as mkt returns to normal.
newsitem.headline: German call money eases as mkt returns to normal.

text.p: German call money rates eased to 3.025/3.075 percent on Wednesday from Tuesday's 3.05/3.15 percent as the money market continued to recover from its end-month stains which had pushed rates up as high as 4.50 marks on Monday.
The fall in money rates came despite a 500 million-mark net drain of funds at the Bundesbank's weekly repo allocation.

Commercial banks' effective deposits at the Bundesbank totalled 40.4 billion marks on Tuesday, down from 46.1 billion on Monday. The daily average on Tuesday was 40.4 billion marks, up from 39.0 billion.
Lombard borrowings on Tuesday plunged to about 100 million marks from 6.8 billion marks on Monday.
The Frankfurt Interbank Overnight Average FIONA= on Wednesday totalled 3.09825 percent, down from 3.12367 percent on Tuesday.
